correctness.rationale: For the prescribed continuous-time reversible generator, stationary-mass-weighted Poisson equations telescope and give H_{i,i+1}=P_i/w_i and H_{i+1,i}=(1-P_i)/w_i. Strong Markov additivity makes the maximal ordered-pair hitting expectation the maximum of the two endpoint directional sums. For each lambda in [0,1], a weighted average and Cauchy-Schwarz yield lower bound S(lambda)^2 and force w_i(lambda)=sqrt(a_i(lambda)/c_i)/S(lambda) at equality. S is strictly concave for n>=3 because not all partial masses P_i equal 1/2; its derivative G/2 is strictly decreasing. At the maximizing scalar lambda*, F-B=S G with correct boundary signs, so the sharp Cauchy bound equals the max objective and the equality allocation is uniquely optimal. Reflection/price cancellation at lambda=1/2 and the symmetric three-state threshold 1/3<=c1/c2<=3 follow by direct substitution. The inspected verify.py independently solves rational Poisson systems in finite cases but is not the proof. All domain restrictions (positive pi,c,w, normalized total mass and cost, no discrete-time rate caps) are needed.
